project.name: Trail Ledger
project.summary: Outdoor groups need a shared trip log that works on phones and in a browser, including poor-connectivity conditions.
project.problem_statement: Outdoor groups need a shared trip log that works on phones and in a browser, including poor-connectivity conditions.
goals: Share trip plans and updates across devices
Keep recent trip details available offline
Make permissions and data ownership clear

facts.value: Outdoor groups need a shared trip log that works on phones and in a browser, including poor-connectivity conditions.

preferences: Flutter or native clients pending comparison

features.name: Trip plans
acceptance_criteria: A trip has members, route notes, and a clear owner

features.name: Offline trip log
acceptance_criteria: Recent trip data remains readable offline
Edits reconcile without silently losing changes

features.name: Member invitations
acceptance_criteria: Invite links expire and can be revoked

architecture.summary: Example architecture outline; validate choices against project requirements and current platform documentation.

components.name: Android and iOS clients
components.description: Present trips and cache recent data

components.name: Trip data store
components.description: Persists members, trips, and revision history

authentication: Email sign-in and group membership roles

decisions.question: Offline edit conflict policy
options: Last writer wins with visible history
decisions.rationale: Prototype both with duplicate concurrent edits and select based on user testing.

security_privacy: Location and trip data require explicit sharing controls
constraints.offline: Trip plans and recent logs must remain readable offline; synchronization policy is a pending decision.
accessibility: Support screen readers and large text across clients
localization: Date, time, and distance units are locale aware
deployment: Use staged rollout and monitored migrations

gaps: supervisor: risk and dependency management is unverified
web-engineer: web frontend engineering is unverified
android-engineer: Android platform knowledge is unverified

supervisor.name: Supervisor / Technical Lead
supervisor.mission: Own the canonical project specification and coordinate delivery.
responsibilities: Maintain scope, manifest, milestones, risks, and decisions
exclusions: Does not own every implementation workstream
Does not present assumptions as verified facts
inputs: Accepted project manifest and relevant repository evidence
Prerequisite: Receives findings from all specialists
Prerequisite: Architecture and product choices precede implementation assignments
acceptance_criteria: All work has an owner and handoff
handoff_requirements: Give bounded briefs with inputs, outputs, and acceptance criteria
Return unresolved user-owned decisions to the user

specialists.name: Web Engineer
specialists.mission: Plan browser and web application architecture.
responsibilities: Recommend component, state, and routing structure
Identify responsive, accessibility, security, and browser constraints
exclusions: Does not decide backend data ownership
Does not claim accessibility conformance without checks
inputs: Accepted project manifest and relevant repository evidence
acceptance_criteria: Routes and data states are covered
responsive and failure states are documented
handoff_requirements: Work with UX and QA on responsive behavior

specialists.name: Android Engineer
specialists.mission: Plan Android application architecture and implementation constraints.
responsibilities: Identify APIs, permissions, lifecycle, compatibility, and release requirements
exclusions: Does not claim device behavior from a manifest alone
Does not own product scope or backend implementation
inputs: Accepted project manifest and relevant repository evidence
handoff_requirements: Coordinate API needs with backend and security

specialists.name: iOS Engineer
specialists.mission: Plan iOS application architecture and platform integration.
responsibilities: Identify entitlement, privacy, lifecycle, accessibility, and release needs
exclusions: Does not infer App Store acceptance
inputs: Accepted project manifest and relevant repository evidence
handoff_requirements: Coordinate backend API and security needs

specialists.name: Backend Engineer
specialists.mission: Plan service architecture, APIs, and business logic.
responsibilities: Define service boundaries and API behavior
Identify reliability, idempotency, and observability needs
exclusions: Does not choose database alone when data modeling is material
Does not treat authentication as authorization
inputs: Accepted project manifest and relevant repository evidence
acceptance_criteria: API contract has consumers, errors, and security requirements
handoff_requirements: Supply contracts to clients and QA

rationale: Web Engineer: project signal matches 'web'; project signal matches 'browser'; selected platform is Web
Android Engineer: project signal matches 'android'; selected platform is Android
iOS Engineer: project signal matches 'ios'; selected platform is iOS
Review 5 overlapping role pair(s); keep separate only if their deliverables have distinct owners.

workstream_independence.basis: 1 minus overlapping role pairs divided by all possible specialist pairs; a one-role team scores 1.0.

coordination_overhead.basis: Team-size, handoff, and project-complexity planning heuristic; lower is simpler.

context_requirements.basis: Planning estimate uses 2,500 supervisor input tokens, 1,500 per specialist, and 120 per feature or architecture component.

research_complexity.basis: Average number of catalogue research methods per selected role, multiplied by 1.5 and capped at 10.

integration_complexity.basis: Heuristic: 1 + 0.75 per specialist + 0.8 per overlap pair + 0.6 per manifest dependency + 0.25 per architecture component, capped at 10.

metrics.review_effort_basis: Uncalibrated points: 2 supervisor points, 1 per specialist, 0.5 per catalogue deliverable, and 0.25 per acceptance criterion.

deliverables.name: Accepted project kickoff specification
acceptance_criteria: Open decisions and risks are visible
Manifest validates and generated documents agree

risks.description: Client divergence may create inconsistent offline behavior
risks.mitigation: Share API contracts and cross-platform acceptance cases

blockers: Resolve the pending project decisions and verify architecture/dependency compatibility.
